'''Rajon Rondo''' (born February 22, 1986 in [[Louisville, Kentucky]]) is  a U.S. basketball player and former point guard for the [[University of Kentucky]]. Rondo is known for his fast offensive pace and tremendous defensive abilities. He left after two seasons at UK and is entering the [[2006 NBA Draft]]. 

== High School == 
Rondo attended Louisville's [[Louisville Eastern High School|Eastern High School]] for three years where he played basketball under head coach Doug Bibby. There, as a junior he averaged 27.6 ppg, 10.0 rpg and 7.5 apg. He also earned All-State honors and was named the 7th Region Player of the Year. He transferred to Virginia's [[Oak Hill Academy]] for his senior year where he averaged 21.0 ppg, 3.0 rpg and 12.0 apg. Rondo was also crowned as a part of [[McDonald’s All-American Team]] in 2004 and scored a total of 14 points, 4 assists and 4 rebounds in the all-star game. He also participated in the 2004 Jordan Capital Classic game, logging 12 points, 5 assists and 4 steals. In his senior year, Rondo dished out 31 assists in a single game, merely four away from the all time national record. He is still in touch with Eastern’s Coach Bibby and maintains a strong friendship with him. 

== College == 
Rondo led Kentucky to several wins including clutch-shot victories against the [[University of Louisville]], [[University of South Carolina|South Carolina]] and [[University of Central Florida|Central Florida]], but Kentucky failed to advance to the Final Four of the [[NCAA Men's Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] in either Rondo's freshman or sophomore seasons. He was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshmen Team. He set the UK single-season record for steals (totaling 87) his freshman year and made at least one steal in every game. In his sophomore year he had a career high 12 assists against [[University of Mississippi|Ole Miss]] and 25 points against Louisville. Rondo also set a UK record for most rebounds in a game by a guard, grabbing 19 rebounds in an early season loss to [[University of Iowa|Iowa]].

Rondo was also named to the 2005 USA Men’s Under-21 World Championship Team, which traveled to [[Argentina]] for the [[FIBA]] World Championships. He averaged 11.0 ppg and 4.5 apg in the eight-game tournament, garnering much attention from NBA scouts. The USA U-21 team won a gold medal at the Global Games held in [[Texas]] in late July.

Most NBA mock drafts project him going in the mid to late first round.

==Personal== 
Rajon is the son of Amber Rondo and has three siblings: Dymon, William, and Anton. He has a prized shoe collection and was majoring in social work. Rondo is very close to former Wildcat [[Derek Anderson]] and drives a car licensed to him.
